messages:
Talia Morris: quick design sync  on the version-history mini-map: current compact mode stacks version chips tightly which is great visually but keyboard scrubbing loses context. On focus you can't tell which chip is selected in the timeline. screenshot: https://img.redwood.dev/mock/version-minimap-compact.png

Rico Alvarez: saw it. When keyboard-navigating we should surface a high-contrast halo and an offscreen label that reads the commit + version date. Users relying on keyboard or VO need clear contextual feedback.

Samir - Eng: implementation note: we can add focus-visible styles and update aria-current on the focused chip. But performance-wise the mini-map renders thousands of points for big histories; we need to virtualize focus regions so SR reads only the active cluster.

Nadia - PM: product ask: when a user scrubs to a past version and triggers rollback, we want a clear safety affordance. Options: (A) inline confirmation tooltip anchored to chip (B) full modal with changelog + impact preview (C) quick confirm microdialog for power users. Thoughts?

Talia Morris: prefer B for destructive rollbacks and C for quick undos. Inline tooltip OK for preview but not for final confirm. Also propose a subtle delay (500ms) on accidental enter to avoid immediate rollbacks when scrubbing via keyboard.

Rico Alvarez: keyboard flow: arrow keys move scrub focus, Enter opens preview tooltip, Shift+Enter opens full rollback modal. Also support Escape to close tooltip. For SR, Enter should announce: "Preview: version X, press Shift+Enter to rollback". Use aria-live region updates.

Samir - Eng: technical: the mini-map is canvas-based currently for perf. Canvas isn't accessible. We should overlay an invisible DOM layer with focusable hotspots for each cluster (or a sparse subset) that map back to canvas coords. That's doable but we must keep event mapping light.

a11y-bot: checklist: focusable hotspots present, visible focus indicator >=3px, aria-current updates on focus, tooltip announcements via aria-live="polite", destructive actions require modal confirmation, reduced-motion respected, keyboard shortcuts documented in help drawer.

Nadia - PM: metrics: timeline_scrub_keyboard, scrub_preview_opened, rollback_modal_opened, rollback_confirmed, accidental_rollback_rate. Goal: reduce accidental_rollback_rate by 80% vs current.

Talia Morris: microcopy for tooltip preview: title "Version 2026-03-18 · v3.4.2" body "Changes: prompt-optimizations, quantization update. Deployed to canary 12%" actions: "Preview traffic" (opens inspector) and tertiary "Rollback" (opens modal). Rollback modal title: "Confirm rollback to v3.4.2" body: short changelog + estimated user impact + undo window. Primary CTA: "Confirm rollback" secondary: "Cancel".

Rico Alvarez: visual: halo color should be accessible (consider deep indigo) and for the mini-map zoom state increase halo thickness from 2px to 4px. Also add a motion cue when selection changes: subtle scale 1.03 -> respect reduced-motion.

Samir - Eng: agree on DOM overlay approach. We'll prototype with sparse hotspots (every Nth chip plus current cluster) and map keyboard left/right to prev/next hotspot. Also implement a debounce for Enter (500ms) before firing heavy actions.

a11y-bot: reminder: any keyboard shortcut needs to be discoverable in the top-right help menu and have accessible hints (aria-describedby).

Talia Morris: action items: 1) I'll update Figma with hotspot overlay visuals, focus halo, and tooltip+modal comps. 2) Samir to prototype DOM-hotspot + debounced confirm in staging. 3) Rico to test contrast + reduced-motion. 4) Nadia to add telemetry and update SLO for accidental rollbacks. Target: next sprint.

Nadia - PM: tagging @samir @rico. Please drop prototypes in the ticket and link the accessibility test plan.

Talia Morris: will upload frames and a short prototype by EOD. thanks everyone :sparkles:
